extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary educational institutions), Title IX Coordinators, institutional administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for institutional compliance with the Department of Education's Title IX final rule, including Title IX Coordinator duties, notification requirements, supportive measures, grievance procedures, training, and pregnancy-related accommodations. Intended to direct recipient policies and implementation decisions across K-12 and postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator Obligations: Duty to Monitor (§ 106.44(b) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should monitor their education programs and activities for barriers to reporting sex discrimination; the Title IX Coordinator role centralizes duties, promotes accountability, and enables effective Title IX compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects flexibility in how recipients implement monitoring consistent with their size and resources. Low-cost monitoring methods include incorporating questions about reporting barriers into existing training materials, and using roundtables or listening sessions. Title IX Coordinators may delegate specific duties to designees but must retain ultimate oversight (see § 106.8(a)). Monitoring, evaluating results, and developing initiatives or training to address barriers are part of this duty; costs were assessed as de minimis in the Department's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification Requirements (§ 106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees with notification duties must take action when they have information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX; recipients must define who those employees are and ensure they act accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elementary and secondary schools must require all non-confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information. For other recipients, two categories exist: (1) employees with authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership/teaching/advising must notify the Title IX Coordinator; (2) other non-confidential employees must either notify the Title IX Coordinator or provide the Coordinator's contact information and complaint instructions. Training on these notification obligations is required under § 106.8(d); notification costs are considered part of training and the cost of an individual employee's notification is de minimis. Recipients may train all non-confidential employees to notify to simplify compliance; training must occur promptly when employees change positions and annually thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Supportive Measures (§ 106.44(f)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures designed to restore or preserve a party's access to the recipient's education program or activity for all forms of sex discrimination; supportive measures must be 'reasonably available.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are available for all forms of sex discrimination per the definition in § 106.2 and § 106.44(a). The Department expects increased instances in which supportive measures are offered under the final regulations and adjusted its economic assumptions (increasing the prior multiplier from 1.5 to 2.0), retained an acceptance rate assumption of 90%, and estimated cost per incident at $250. Supportive measures aim to ensure nondiscriminatory access and are considered part of recipients' obligations to address sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial Review of Supportive Measures (§ 106.44(g)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an appropriate, impartial employee to consider challenges to supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement does not mandate a full administrative structure; at minimum, assign one person to handle challenged decisions. The Department estimates negligible monetary cost per incident and de minimis cumulative annual costs. The independent review requirement is justified by its importance to fairness despite any minimal burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance Procedures Core Requirements (§§ 106.45 and 106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must ensure fair, transparent, and reliable outcomes through procedural safeguards including notice of allegations, an opportunity to respond, an adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation, and an objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional procedures apply for allegations of sex-based harassment involving a postsecondary student. The Department emphasizes that these core requirements protect due process for both complainants and respondents. The regulations balance procedural rigor with recipient discretion to implement cost-effective approaches consistent with Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance Procedures: Recipient Flexibility and Streamlining
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain discretion over the design and implementation of grievance procedures within the regulatory requirements, allowing flexibility to reduce administrative burdens while maintaining fair outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibilities include setting reasonable timeframes, using institutional employees or contractors as investigators/decisionmakers, choosing an individual decisionmaker or panel, offering informal resolution options, selecting disciplinary sanctions, and determining appeal procedures. The final regulations remove or make permissive several 2020 prescriptive requirements (e.g., live hearing mandate, prohibition on single-investigator model, mandatory investigative report), enabling streamlining without sacrificing efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Stability and Reliance Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department considered reliance interests in existing policies and collective bargaining agreements and sought to preserve stability by retaining and enhancing many 2020 requirements or making certain provisions permissive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department recognized potential need to renegotiate collective bargaining agreements, it determined that benefits of final regulations justify such burdens. The final rules were crafted to balance clarity and stability with necessary changes to better effectuate Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Decisionmakers (§ 106.46(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must receive training consistent with the final regulations to ensure equitable, transparent, and reliable grievance outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients were already required to train decisionmakers under the 2020 amendments; the content will be adjusted under the final rule but is unlikely to lengthen training substantially. Any administrative cost is justified by the benefits of improved grievance procedure quality. See § 106.8(d) for further detail on training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Investigator Model (§ 106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are permitted to use a single-investigator model for investigating and deciding certain sex discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single-investigator model may shorten timelines, allow the investigator with the most knowledge to decide, and increase scheduling efficiency. The Department concluded permitting the model supports quality grievance procedures and can increase students' willingness to seek institutional support; recipients may elect to use it as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy or Related Conditions: Reasonable Modifications (§§ 106.40 and 106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide reasonable modifications to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement clarifies and builds upon prior 'reasonable and responsive' standards. Examples of reasonable modifications include allowing a larger desk, more frequent bathroom breaks, or temporary elevator access. The Department does not anticipate significant new costs because many obligations are longstanding; any minimal additional costs are outweighed by benefits of access and prevention of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy or Related Conditions: Lactation Space Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make lactation spaces available to students and employees that meet minimum acceptable standards of privacy, sanitation, and functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement for a specific number, size, or features beyond privacy, cleanliness, and that the space not be a bathroom. Many recipients already provide similar spaces for employees under the PUMP Act. A recipient without a designated space is likely able to comply using existing space; retrofits (e.g., keypad lock, chair) would be minimal cost. Lactation spaces need not be available 24/7 and may be shared or repurposed as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy or Related Conditions: Scope Limited to Pregnant Students
rubrics_metrics.description: Required reasonable modifications apply only to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, not to partners, family members, or others who are not pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explicitly limited the regulatory obligation to pregnant students; costs of modifications for others were not analyzed because they are not imposed by the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Requirement to Provide or Pay for Abortion-Related Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.40 and 106.57(e) do not require a recipient to provide or pay for any benefit, service, or facility related to abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about abortion-related costs are unfounded under the final regulations; the Department clarifies that pregnancy-related accommodations do not include abortion provision or payment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Sex Discrimination (§ 106.10) — Inclusion and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations clarify the scope of Title IX to provide nondiscrimination protections on the basis of sex, including gender identity, and the Department determined that the non-monetary benefits of this clarity justify any associated implementation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered commenters' concerns about increased complaints and costs but concluded clarity in scope and robust protections are warranted. Recipients that previously limited policies to bases referenced in the 2020 amendments may see increased application; benefits across all individuals on the basis of sex justify the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Costs and Administrative Burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assesses certain costs (training, monitoring, supportive measures, Title IX Coordinator duties) and treats some impacts as de minimis, while allowing recipients discretion to implement cost-effective approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs associated with notification are treated as part of training expenses; the cost to notify the Title IX Coordinator is de minimis. The Department revised estimates (e.g., supportive measures multiplier and cost per incident) in its Regulatory Impact Analysis. Recipients may reduce burdens by training all non-confidential employees to notify, using existing staff or contractors, and implementing flexible grievance procedures consistent with regulatory requirements.
